title: Caddy host-derived document roots can be escaped through dot segments or slashes in Host or :authority
summary: A site that builds its document root from the request host can let unauthenticated clients choose paths outside the intended tree. HTTP/1 accepts dot-only Host values; HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 accept slash or backslash characters in :authority. Caddy then cleans the expanded root, allowing file_server to expose filesystem files or PHP handlers to execute files outside the intended directory. The advisory limits exposure to catch-all or on-demand TLS sites using a host-derived root; explicitly listed host names are not affected.
ai_role: The primary Caddy advisory directly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner as discovering the finding under ANT-2026-YKIEF8GR, and contains a proof of concept, impact, patch, and affected configuration conditions. Anthropic’s primary scanner page establishes model-based scanner provenance; the item advisory does not name a model.
classification_note: The primary maintainer published GHSA-r766-rf9f-588h on 2026-11-04 and directly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-YKIEF8GR). For filelock, the source records private scanner report receipt on Oct 15; the public advisory attribution date remains Oct 17.
remediation_note: Caddy 2.11.8 validates Host and :authority consistently across protocols and rejects host values that consist only of dots.
